evals.prompt: Open a sandboxed browser, navigate to https://example.com, get the page title, take a full page screenshot, then stop the browser.
evals.expected_output: Uses Browser Control scripts from scripts/ in order: start, nav, eval, screenshot, stop. Does not use a domain-specific helper.
expectations: The answer uses Browser Control scripts from scripts/ for launch, navigation, evaluation, screenshot, and stop.
The answer does not require a named local Chrome profile unless the user asks for logged-in access.
The answer passes the reported port and owner token to follow-up commands.
Any newly opened tab is opened in the background or through helpers that open background tabs.

evals.prompt: I want to inspect a logged-in website with my normal Chrome account, but I do not want you touching my live Chrome profile. Start a safe browser session and explain where the copied profile lives.
evals.expected_output: Uses Browser Tools managed Chrome with --profile and optionally --sync, explains copied profile and cache defaults, and avoids main Chrome.
expectations: The answer uses scripts/start.mjs with --profile and recommends --sync when current cookies matter.
The answer explains that the live Chrome profile is copied into the configured Browser Tools cache directory.
The answer mentions the default cache path ~/.cache/pi-browser-tools or the configurable cacheDir setting.
The answer does not connect to unmanaged Chrome or the main Chrome profile.

evals.prompt: I need you to open several pages in the browser and scrape data, but please do not steal focus from my desktop while you do it.
evals.expected_output: Uses Browser Control or generic extractors in a way that opens new tabs in the background and avoids bringToFront unless explicitly requested.
expectations: The answer prefers background tab creation with browser.newPage({ background: true }) or existing Browser Control helpers that do this.
The answer avoids page.bringToFront() unless the user explicitly asks to see or interact with the tab.
The answer reminds follow-up commands to use the reported managed browser port when multiple instances exist.

evals.prompt: Extract the article text from the current browser tab and save up to 6000 characters. If no browser is running, tell me exactly what to start first.
evals.expected_output: Uses the generic article extraction helper after a managed browser is running and points to start.mjs when no managed browser exists.
expectations: The answer uses scripts/extract-article.mjs --chars 6000 for current-page extraction.
The answer treats the helper as generic page extraction, not a domain-specific workflow.
The answer tells the user to start Browser Tools with scripts/start.mjs if no managed browser is running.
The answer passes --port and --owner-token or BROWSER_TOOLS_OWNER_TOKEN.

evals.prompt: Set up Browser Tools so my finance task uses a specific Chrome profile by default, but keep the profile name out of the repo.
evals.expected_output: Stores the task profile preference through Browser Tools config under ~/.agents/browser-tools/config.json and starts with --task finance.
expectations: The answer uses scripts/config.mjs task-profile set finance --profile <profile-or-alias>.
The answer uses scripts/start.mjs --task finance for later starts.
The answer explains that task profile preferences live in private Browser Tools config, not repo files.
The answer mentions the default config path ~/.agents/browser-tools/config.json.

evals.prompt: I need current oil and stock index prices. Should I use Browser Tools directly?
evals.expected_output: Routes finance-specific data work to the finance skill instead of adding finance helpers to Browser Tools.
expectations: The answer says Browser Tools is the generic browser layer.
The answer routes finance-specific quote or market data workflows to the finance skill.
The answer explains that the finance skill should call Browser Tools managed Chrome if browser access is needed.

evals.prompt: Record the multi-step login flow in the current managed browser so I can visually inspect it later.
evals.expected_output: Records the active tab through the public record-gif CLI, captures frames before and after browser actions, saves an action-specific GIF filename, and reviews sampled frames as a contact sheet.
expectations: The answer starts with browser-tools record-gif start before the first login action and stops with browser-tools record-gif stop after the final action.
The answer passes an explicit meaningful output filename such as login_process.gif rather than a generic recording.gif name.
The answer explains that start captures pre-action frames and stop captures post-action frames for smooth playback.
The answer passes the reported managed browser port and uses the owner token from the environment.
After recording, the answer runs browser-tools review-gif and inspects the contact sheet for initial, action, and final states.

evals.prompt: Open our checkout page in the managed browser, capture only XHR and Fetch calls under /api while I complete a checkout, and produce something another agent can inspect before writing a replay script.
evals.expected_output: Records an owner-protected filtered HAR around the interaction, then extracts a private redacted chronological network recipe without executing requests.
expectations: The answer starts browser-tools record-har before the interaction and stops it afterward using the reported port and owner token environment.
The HAR command uses an interaction-specific filename and filters to XHR and Fetch plus the requested /api URL pattern.
The answer runs browser-tools extract-har after capture to create an agent-readable chronological recipe.
The answer explains that secrets are redacted by default and --include-sensitive is an explicit private opt-in.
The answer does not execute or replay captured checkout requests and warns that a future script needs side-effect and dynamic-auth review.
